2026-09-12T20:15:06.7537065Z 
2026-09-12T20:15:06.7537177Z To create a pull request:
2026-09-12T20:15:06.7537493Z 1. Make any file changes directly in the working directory.
2026-09-12T20:15:06.7538182Z 2. If you haven't done so already, create a new local branch using `git checkout -b <branch-name>` with an appropriate unique name.
2026-09-12T20:15:06.7540451Z 3. Add and commit your changes to the branch. Be careful to add exactly the files you intend, and check there are no extra files left un-added. Verify you haven't deleted or changed any files you didn't intend to.
2026-09-12T20:15:06.7541369Z 4. Do not push your changes. That will be done by the tool.
2026-09-12T20:15:06.7542070Z 5. Create the pull request with the create_pull_request tool from safeoutputs exactly once, only when the final title/body/branch are ready.
2026-09-12T20:15:06.7543067Z 6. After calling `create_pull_request`, STOP. Do not probe with another PR call, do not test auth with manual `git push`, and do not rewrite git remotes.
2026-09-12T20:15:06.7543608Z

2026-09-12T20:15:06.7554455Z 
2026-09-12T20:15:06.7555359Z For `safeoutputs`, every successful call is a real write-intent declaration - do not use it for probing, auth checks, or placeholder payloads. Use `noop` or `report_incomplete` if not ready to emit the final action.
2026-09-12T20:15:06.7556125Z 
2026-09-12T20:15:06.7556402Z For multiple or complex arguments, pipe a JSON object on stdin using `.` as the sentinel:
2026-09-12T20:15:06.7556837Z ```bash
2026-09-12T20:15:06.7557182Z printf '{"item_number":42,"body":"### Title\n\nBody."}' | safeoutputs add_comment .
2026-09-12T20:15:06.7557714Z # or write to a file: safeoutputs create_pull_request . < /tmp/payload.json
2026-09-12T20:15:06.7558098Z ```
2026-09-12T20:15:06.7558202Z 
2026-09-12T20:15:06.7560171Z **Multi-line or long `body` content:** do NOT build the JSON payload with `printf`/`echo` embedding raw newlines or many escaped characters directly in the command line — the sandbox's shell command-injection guard may reject long or complex quoted arguments (reporting "expansion patterns"/"command substitution" even though none are present) and retrying the identical command will fail again. Instead, write the content to a temp file with a heredoc, then use `jq -Rs` to inject it as the `body` field:
2026-09-12T20:15:06.7561966Z ```bash
2026-09-12T20:15:06.7562187Z cat <<'EOF' > /tmp/gh-aw/body.md
2026-09-12T20:15:06.7562443Z Title
2026-09-12T20:15:06.7562555Z 
2026-09-12T20:15:06.7562669Z Multi-line body content goes here.
2026-09-12T20:15:06.7562923Z EOF
2026-09-12T20:15:06.7563278Z jq -Rs '{title: "My title", body: .}' /tmp/gh-aw/body.md | safeoutputs create_discussion .
2026-09-12T20:15:06.7563820Z ```
2026-09-12T20:15:06.7564476Z If a shell command is rejected for containing expansion patterns, do not retry the same command — switch to the heredoc + `jq -Rs` pattern above.
2026-09-12T20:15:06.7565191Z 
2026-09-12T20:15:06.7565577Z To inject an entire local file as the `body` field without re-embedding its content in the model context, use `jq -Rs`:
2026-09-12T20:15:06.7566121Z ```bash
2026-09-12T20:15:06.7566383Z jq -Rs --arg discussion_number "$DISCUSSION_NUMBER" \
2026-09-12T20:15:06.7566799Z   '{discussion_number: ($discussion_number|tonumber), body: .}' \
2026-09-12T20:15:06.7567166Z   discussion-body.md \
2026-09-12T20:15:06.7567432Z   | safeoutputs update_discussion .
2026-09-12T20:15:06.7567697Z ```
2026-09-12T20:15:06.7568491Z `jq -Rs` reads the file as a raw string (`-R`) and slurps it into a single JSON string value (`-s`), so `body` is always a valid JSON field. Piping `cat file | safeoutputs ...` does not populate `body` and will be rejected.
2026-09-12T20:15:06.7569240Z
